page: Amazon Web Services r7i.48xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by Intel Xeon 8488C processors operating at a nominal clock speed of 3.2 GHz, the system exposes 192 vCPUs across 96 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation totals 1536.0 GB of DDR5 RAM running at 5 GHz, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The configuration contains no dedicated GPUs and features zero local instance storage, requiring all persistent and scratch volumes to rely on network-attached options. Network throughput provides a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant compute capacity under heavy parallel loads. The 192-vCPU architecture achieves a multi-core stress-ng result of 169,761.83 and a PassMark CPU score of 123,948.44, both placing in the top 10% tier. Instruction extensions such as AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8 enhance vectorized execution, as evidenced by a PassMark extended instructions score of 192,232.65. Single-core performance falls largely within typical enterprise baselines, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2,016.29 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2,072.0.

The 1.5 TB DDR5 memory subsystem offers substantial throughput, delivering 454.59 GB/sec uncached large-block reads and 190.44 GB/sec large-block writes. This high-capacity memory architecture translates directly to strong in-memory key-value performance, achieving 183.87 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads. For CPU-based machine learning inference, the platform delivers 2,700.02 tokens/sec during prompt processing on a 135M model, tapering to 37.79 tokens/sec prompt processing and 5.42 tokens/sec text generation on a 70B parameter model.

Cost efficiency is focused primarily on large-scale memory consolidation. The massive vCPU density and large RAM footprint allow organizations to run expansive memory footprints on a single hypervisor instance without multi-node sharding overhead. However, the complete absence of local NVMe storage requires careful consideration of network I/O overhead and external storage costs for disk-intensive workflows. The instance is suited for enterprise in-memory databases, large Redis clusters, high-scale SAP or SQL deployments, extensive Clang software compilation, and big data analytics pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r7i.48xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 192 vCPUs (96 physical cores) based on 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8488C processors and 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory. Utilizing the Nitro hypervisor architecture, it provides a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps, and no local disk storage or GPUs. The platform exhibits high-tier multi-threaded performance, yielding a stress-ng multi-core score of 169,761.83 and a PassMark CPU score of 123,948.44, alongside AMX and AVX-512 instruction support. Memory operations reach 454.59 GB/sec on uncached reads and 183.87 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. This hardware profile provides resource density for enterprise memory consolidation, making it well suited for large-scale in-memory databases, distributed caching, massive software compilation, and data analytics pipelines.
